fix: resolve XRT libs from multiarch mirror for XRT >= 2.25

XRT 2.25 changed Linux runtime library discovery: get_xilinx_xrt() now
ignores $XILINX_XRT and instead uses dladdr() on libxrt_coreutil.so to
find where the loader resolved it from, then strips the XRT_LIB_DIR
suffix (lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, two components) to recover the XRT root.

The portable tree ships the real libxrt_coreutil.so in $SCRIPT_DIR/lib
and pointed LD_LIBRARY_PATH there, so 2.25 stripped two components from
".../lib" and derived the PARENT of the release dir as the root, failing
with:
  No such library '<parent>/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libxrt_core.so.2'

Prepend the multiarch mirror ($SCRIPT_DIR/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu) to
LD_LIBRARY_PATH so libxrt_coreutil.so resolves from there; dladdr() then
reports that path and stripping two components yields $SCRIPT_DIR. Also
make the mirror symlink creation idempotent instead of gated on the dir
being absent. $XILINX_XRT is still exported for the pre-2.25 scheme, so
the change is backward compatible.

fix: write FLM_MODEL_PATH as a per-user env var in the MSI installer

FLM_MODEL_PATH was written as a machine-wide (HKLM) Environment entry
containing the literal "%USERPROFILE%\.flm". USERPROFILE is a per-user
variable, so a machine-wide reference to it resolves against SYSTEM's
own profile in some contexts, producing
C:\Windows\system32\config\systemprofile\.flm, which a real user can't
write to ("create_directories: Access is denied.").

Write it per-user (HKCU) instead: each user has their own HKCU, so
"%USERPROFILE%\.flm" only ever needs to resolve correctly for the one
user it's stored under, and Windows expands it lazily when that
user's session environment is built. Also exposed as a command-line
override (FLMMODELPATH=<dir>) for unattended SYSTEM-context installs.

fix: report full prompt length in OpenAI usage

The prompt cache erases the matching prefix from `tokens` before prefill, so
`meta_info.prompt_tokens = tokens.size()` recorded only the newly evaluated
suffix. The first turn of a conversation has no cache and looked correct, but
every later turn reused the whole history as a cached prefix and reported just
the new message.

OpenAI defines usage.prompt_tokens as the entire input, with cached tokens
counted inside it and broken out separately. Reporting the delta instead made
the context appear to reset on every request, so clients that size the context
from usage never learn how full it is -- an agent front-end deciding when to
compact from that figure never compacts.

Add the erased prefix back into prompt_tokens, carry the cached count on
chat_meta_info_t, and expose it as usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens on
the OpenAI endpoints. prefill_speed_tps now divides by the tokens actually
evaluated, so a cache hit no longer inflates it.

The Ollama-compatible prompt_eval_count is left reporting evaluated tokens
only, matching upstream Ollama.

ci(sweep): stream sweep progress instead of buffering it until exit

A sweep runs for tens of minutes and its stdout is the only live indication
of what it is doing, but Python block-buffers stdout whenever it is not a
terminal. Under Actions that meant every print sat in an 8 KB buffer and
arrived in one burst at job end: the log showed a single server_start line
and then nothing until the sweep was over.

The per-request output already existed -- the model header, the prompt for
each round, the timing line. Only log_event passed flush=True, which is why
that one line appeared live and nothing else did. Rather than add flush=True
to the other 55 prints and have to remember it in every new one, line-buffer
stdout/stderr once at import; that covers all four task scripts.

Also print position and elapsed time per model from iter_models, the single
point every task funnels through, so a watcher can tell how far along a
40-model sweep is rather than only which model is current.

ci(sweep): report the server's prefill/decode breakdown per request

"done in 20.08s, 117 chars" cannot distinguish a slow prefill from a slow
decode, which is most of what a model sweep is trying to find out. FLM
already reports the split; the sweep was discarding it.

Its final streaming chunk carries a usage block well beyond the OpenAI
standard (src/server/streaming_ostream_openai.hpp send_final_response):
prompt and completion tokens, cached prompt tokens, separate prefill and
decode durations and rates, model load duration, and KV occupancy. The
non-streaming response carries the same. chat() now keeps it on last_usage
and format_usage() renders it:

  done in 20.08s, 117 chars
    prefill 1234 tok (12 cached) in 0.83s @ 1477.6 tps | decode 117 tok in
    19.25s @ 6.1 tps | load 0.42s | kv 1351/8192 (16%)

collect_stream had to read usage before its "if not chunk.choices: continue"
guard. FLM's final chunk carries both a null-delta choices entry and the
usage, so the guard did not drop it, but a server using the stock OpenAI
shape sends usage on a chunk with no choices at all and would have been
missed.

No stream_options/include_usage is sent: FLM emits usage unconditionally,
and asking for it could only break servers that do not know the option.
Every field is treated as optional, so a server reporting only the standard
counts degrades to "prefill N tok | decode N tok" and one reporting nothing
leaves the plain timing line untouched.

ci(sweep): treat single-turn models' refused follow-up as expected

model_list.json labels four models "single-turn" -- hy-mt2:1.8b,
qwen3vl-flash:4b, gemma4e-flash:e2b and :e4b. They are built for one
exchange and cap context at 1k, so the llm and vision sweeps' second round
was being rejected by design and then counted as a model failure. The sweep
was reporting correct behaviour as a defect.

`flm list --json` already carries the label: main.cpp copies each whole
model_list.json entry into the output, so nothing had to change on the
server side. The catalog now keeps the label array, and the follow-up round
is skipped for anything marked single-turn.

Skipped rather than sent-and-tolerated: the round is known to be rejected,
so sending it only spends NPU time on a request whose failure would have to
be filtered out afterwards anyway.

The round is still written to the CSV, with status "skipped" and the reason,
and the models are listed in the summary JSON and the job summary. A reader
can see a test was deliberately shortened rather than silently losing a
round.

Models with no label are treated as multi-turn. /v1/models carries no
labels, so assuming single-turn on unknown models would quietly drop the
follow-up for every model whenever the flm binary was unavailable.
